items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: So he finally got the idea of forming his own band... So as we went on it started taking effect. And we ended up with a pretty good band with Earl.

ctx.x: Well how long were you with Charlie Echols?

Oh, I stayed with Ecc for a long time until a fellow came to California named Earl Dancer. He'd just come from New York. He used to be Ethel Waters' manager. And he had some big ideas. He was a good talker and a good promoter. And he went right into the studios and then he, he used to get all the studio work for bands. He knew some of the big shots that had been in New York and now they were stars in the studios.
So when they saw Earl, he could get a lot of jobs that Echols couldn't get. So he finally got the idea of forming his own band and keeping the band working in the studios making pretty good money.
